hol6: 💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated; the sliced chicken, rice and bean salsa freeze well for up to 3 months, but leave the yogurt ranch out as it splits once frozen.
💡 Pull the chicken out at 74°C on a probe rather than trusting the 28 minutes — thick breasts vary, and overcooked breast is what makes reheated BBQ chicken chalky.
m13: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and the beef-pepper mix freezes for 3 months; store the chipotle sauce in a small pot so the rice does not turn gluey underneath it.
💡 Reheat at 70% microwave power with a splash of water over the rice, then add the blended sauce cold — cottage cheese and yogurt go grainy if boiled.
m02: 💡 Eats best within 3 days because the pickles and spinach soften; freezing is not recommended as the yogurt sauce weeps and the pasta turns mushy on thawing.
💡 Rinse the drained pasta briefly under cold water before folding in the sauce — cool pasta and cool beef are what stop the yogurt curdling into grainy bits.
hol4: 💡 This chilli keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes for 3 months in single portions; it tastes better on day two once the chipotle has mellowed into the pumpkin.
💡 Reheat on the hob or at full microwave power until steaming, then add the lime and any yogurt afterwards — lime goes bitter and yogurt splits when heated.
m09: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze without the celery and bacon if you can, as celery turns limp and the bacon loses its crunch once thawed.
💡 Cook the beef bacon separately and keep it in a small pot to scatter on after reheating at 60% microwave power, otherwise it turns chewy sitting in the sauce.
m28: 💡 Assemble and toast, then cool fully before wrapping individually in foil; they keep 4 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen, and reheat best in an air fryer at 180°C for 8 minutes.
💡 Keep the lettuce and mayo sauce in separate pots and tuck them in after reheating — hot lettuce goes slimy and the mayonnaise-based sauce splits in the microwave.
m38: 💡 Cauliflower rice releases water as it sits, so eat within 3 days and reheat uncovered in a hot pan for 3–4 minutes rather than microwaving, which steams it into mush.
💡 Use frozen cauliflower rice straight from the bag without thawing and give it space in the pan — a crowded, wet pan boils it instead of frying it.
m45: 💡 Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes well for 3 months; the lentils thicken to a stew overnight, so loosen each portion with 50–100 mL of water when reheating.
💡 Stick to the 10-minute natural release — quick-releasing a lentil-heavy pot can spit starchy liquid through the valve and leaves the chicken breasts stringier.
m14: 💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated; portions freeze acceptably for 2 months but the broccoli softens, so undercook it slightly if you plan to freeze the batch.
💡 Add the pasta al dente and no earlier than the final 15 minutes — pasta left in a slow cooker on high keeps drinking sauce and turns pasty by day two.
m12: 💡 Refrigerate up to 4 days; the blended cottage cheese sauce freezes without splitting, so this is one of the better pasta dishes to stash in the freezer for 2 months.
💡 Blend the cheese sauce for the full 4–5 minutes and stir it in with the slow cooker on low — the honey and milk scorch on the base if it stays on high.
m18: 💡 Keeps 3 days in the fridge; do not freeze, as the yogurt-espresso sauce separates on thawing and the chicken breasts dry out. Reheat gently at 50% power.
💡 The heat must be fully off before the yogurt goes in — pour it over a bubbling pan and it will curdle. Take the chicken off at 74°C to keep it juicy.
m07: 💡 Refrigerate for 4 days; the shredded chicken and rice freeze well for 3 months, but the corn-pico mix and sour cream should stay fresh in a separate pot.
💡 Shred the chicken while it is still warm in the cooker liquid, then drain — shredding cold, drained breast gives dry strands that never soak the chipotle sauce back up.
m26: 💡 Best eaten within 3 days; freezing makes the flank steak tough and the Gruyère sauce grainy. Reheat at 60% microwave power with a splash of water, stirring halfway.
💡 Sear the flank steak no further than medium-rare and dice it only at the end — it gets a second cook in the sauce, and well-done flank turns to shoe leather.
m05: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 2 months; the caramelised onion sauce reheats well on the hob with a few spoons of stock to loosen it.
💡 Give the onions the full 45 minutes and only add stock once they stick — rushing them on high heat gives bitter, burnt edges rather than deep sweetness.
m10: 💡 Refrigerate up to 4 days; freezes for 2 months, though steam the broccoli only until bright green if freezing, as it goes soft on the second reheat.
💡 Bring the cream cheese to room temperature before it goes in the slow cooker — cold blocks leave stubborn lumps that never fully melt into the milk.
m11: 💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes for 2 months in single portions; reheat on the hob with a splash of stock rather than drying it out in the microwave.
💡 Par-cooking the spaghetti to half time is the whole trick — fully cooked pasta added to the slow cooker for 30 minutes turns into a soft, gluey block.
hol9: 💡 Refrigerate 3–4 days; the mash and broccoli freeze fine, but sliced steak reheated from frozen goes grey and tough, so keep the steak portion fresh.
💡 Reheat the mash and broccoli fully, then add the steak slices for only the last 30 seconds at 50% power — or eat them cold — and spoon the yogurt sauce on after.
m39: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the turkey-bean mix freezes for 3 months, and the rice can share the container as long as it is cooled quickly before sealing.
💡 Turkey mince dries out faster than beef, so keep it moving, tip in the tomatoes as soon as it loses its pink, and keep the lime wedges separate until serving.
m51: 💡 Refrigerate up to 3 days; fried rice freezes well for a month, but the seared steak cubes are best kept fresh, and the yum-yum sauce must stay in its own pot.
💡 Reheat in a hot wok or pan for 3 minutes rather than the microwave — the pan re-crisps the rice, and cold day-old rice is exactly what keeps the grains separate.
m54: 💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated; the beef and rice freeze well for 3 months, but the cherry tomatoes and cottage cheese topping should be added fresh on the day.
💡 Brown the mince in two batches so it fries rather than steams grey — crowding 1.3 kg into one pan releases water and you lose the smoky paprika crust.
m55: 💡 Eat within 4 days; roasted sweet potato cubes reheat far better in an air fryer at 190°C for 5 minutes than in the microwave, which turns them soft and wet.
💡 Spread the sweet potato in a single layer with space between cubes — a heaped tray steams them into mash rather than giving crisp, caramelised edges.
m58: 💡 Keeps 5 days refrigerated and the chilli freezes for 3 months; store the roasted sweet potato alongside rather than folded in if you want it to keep its texture.
💡 Simmer the passata uncovered so it thickens, then add the spinach at the very end — wilting it earlier leaches water and dulls it to khaki by day three.
m60: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge; quinoa and chicken freeze well, but the courgette goes watery after freezing, so eat frozen portions with fresh veg instead.
💡 Rest the quinoa off the heat for 5 minutes with the lid on before fluffing, and cook the courgette hard and fast in a single layer so it browns rather than weeps.
m61: 💡 Eggs turn rubbery on reheating, so eat within 3 days and warm at 50% microwave power in 45-second bursts, stopping as soon as the rice is hot.
💡 Pull the scrambled eggs off the heat while still glossy and slightly wet — they finish cooking in the residual heat and again at reheat, so undercooked now means tender later.
m06: 💡 Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze for 3 months; the blended cottage cheese sauce holds up in the freezer better than a cream-based one, so this batch is freezer-friendly.
💡 Reheat at 70% power with the lid ajar and stir halfway — the honey-chipotle sauce catches and scorches at the edges if microwaved on full.
m16: 💡 Cool the filling fully before rolling — warm filling steams the wrap and makes it tear. Toasted burritos keep 4 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen wrapped in foil.
💡 Reheat from the fridge in an air fryer at 180°C for 6–8 minutes for a crisp shell; from frozen, microwave 2 minutes first, then air fry to finish.
m22: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the beef freezes well for 3 months, but roasted Brussels sprouts go sulphurous and soft after freezing, so keep those portions fresh.
💡 Add the honey only once the beef is fully browned and the pan is off high heat — it burns in seconds on a dry hot pan and turns bitter rather than sticky.
m15: 💡 Refrigerate up to 4 days; the beef and carrots freeze well, but the potatoes go mealy when frozen, so freeze the meat portion alone and add fresh potato later.
💡 Sit the potatoes on top of the beef rather than under it so they steam instead of boiling in the broth — that keeps them from collapsing into the gravy.
m08: 💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes for 2 months; the pasta will keep absorbing the stock, so stir in 50 mL of water before reheating each portion.
💡 Stir the pasta every few minutes while it cooks in the stock — elbow pasta sinks and welds to the base of the pot, giving a scorched layer under the sauce.
m30: 💡 Keep the chopped iceberg and Greek yogurt in separate pots and toss them in just before eating; the beef, rice, beans and corn base keeps 4 days in the fridge.
💡 Eat this cold or warm only the beef-rice base — 45 seconds at full power is enough — because the cheddar and pico go greasy and watery if the whole bowl is microwaved.
m33: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and the turkey-vegetable mix freezes well for 3 months; the courgette softens a little on thawing, but the tomato base covers it.
💡 99/1 turkey has almost no fat to protect it, so brown it in small batches, do not let it go past pale gold, and let the broth and tomatoes do the rest.
m01: 💡 Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze for 3 months — the cottage cheese and yogurt sauce reheats without splitting because it was blended smooth rather than stirred in cold.
💡 Slow cooker chicken breast dries out past 3 hours on high, so check at 2.5 hours; it should shred with light pressure from a fork, not fall apart into fibres.
m03: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freezes for 2 months, though the pasta softens, so cook it a minute under al dente if you plan to freeze the batch.
💡 Reheat at 60% microwave power with a tablespoon of water over each portion — the sun-dried tomato sauce turns thick and pasty when blasted on full.
m23: 💡 Keep the cream cheese sauce on the lowest heat and stir constantly once it goes in — it splits into grainy specks if it bubbles hard with the pizza sauce.
💡 Reheat in an oven-safe dish at 180°C for 15 minutes with foil loosely on top for a proper pizza-bake finish; the cheese re-melts far better than in the microwave.
m49: 💡 Prawns and avocado are the shortest-lived ingredients here, so eat within 2–3 days and never freeze this assembled — the avocado browns and the prawns turn spongy.
💡 Store the avocado, mango and lime-chilli dressing in a separate pot, and eat the bowl cold or warm only the prawns and rice for 60 seconds so the prawns stay tender.
